question: Which British policy promoted English education to create a loyal class serving British interests in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Education Policy
Subsidiary Alliance
Divide and Rule
Trade Policy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Education Policy

Explanation:
The British government adopted the 'Education Policy' to promote English education in India, aiming to create a loyal and educated class that would assist in British administration. This policy was primarily based on Macaulay's Minute (1835), which prioritized Western education over traditional Indian learning. By providing education in English, the British planned to develop a 'middle class' loyal to British interests. This class was intended to strengthen British rule and spread British values in Indian society. Other options like 'Subsidiary Alliance' and 'Divide and Rule' were political policies, while 'Trade Policy' was related to economic objectives.

☛ What was the main objective of Macaulay's Minute (1835)? → To promote English education and create a loyal class in India
☛ Which language was prioritized under British education policy? → English
☛ What type of class did the education policy aim to create? → Middle class
☛ What is 'Subsidiary Alliance' associated with? → Treaties with Indian princely states
☛ What was the purpose of 'Divide and Rule'? → To promote Hindu-Muslim division
question_hi: भारत में ब्रिटिश हितों की सेवा करने वाले एक वफादार वर्ग को बनाने के लिए किस ब्रिटिश नीति ने अंग्रेजी शिक्षा को बढ़ावा दिया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
ब्रिटिश सरकार ने भारत में अंग्रेजी शिक्षा को बढ़ावा देने के लिए 'शिक्षा नीति' अपनाई, जिसका उद्देश्य एक वफादार और शिक्षित वर्ग तैयार करना था जो ब्रिटिश प्रशासन में सहायक हो। यह नीति मुख्यतः मैकाले के मिनट (1835) पर आधारित थी, जिसमें पश्चिमी शिक्षा को भारतीय परंपरागत शिक्षा पर प्राथमिकता दी गई। अंग्रेजी माध्यम से शिक्षा देकर ब्रिटिश हितों के प्रति वफादार 'मध्यम वर्ग' बनाने की योजना थी। इस वर्ग का उपयोग ब्रिटिश शासन को मजबूत करने और भारतीय समाज में ब्रिटिश मूल्यों को फैलाने के लिए किया जाना था। अन्य विकल्प जैसे 'सहायक गठबंधन' और 'फूट डालो और शासन करो' राजनीतिक नीतियाँ थीं, जबकि 'व्यापार नीति' आर्थिक उद्देश्यों से संबंधित थी।

question: Who among the following had given the idea to mobilise all the leading Indian political leaders under a common platform called the Indian National Congress? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: A O Hume
W C Bannerjee
Surendranath Bannerjee
Ananda Mohan Bose
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A O Hume

Explanation:
The idea of forming the Indian National Congress (INC) was given by A O Hume, a retired British civil servant. He envisioned bringing together all major Indian political leaders under a common platform to present Indian grievances to the government. In 1885, the first session of INC was held in Bombay under the presidency of W C Bannerjee. Hume is regarded as the founder of the INC and served as its General Secretary from 1885 to 1908. Surendranath Bannerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose were also early leaders, but the idea originated with Hume.

☛ What was A O Hume's profession? → Retired British civil servant

question: Which of the following statements regarding the Ryotwari settlement is correct?1.It was developed by Thomas Munro.2. The settlement was made directly with the cultivators, not zamindars.3.It was tested on a small scale in the annexed territories of Tipu.4. Finding it successful, it was then applied in the Ganga plains.Select the correct combination: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1 and 2 only
1 only
1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2, 3 and 4
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1, 2 and 3 only

Explanation:
The Ryotwari settlement was developed by Thomas Munro, where revenue was collected directly from the cultivators, bypassing zamindars. It was first tested on a small scale in the territories annexed from Tipu Sultan. However, this system was confined to southern India and was not applied in the Ganga plains, where the Permanent Settlement and Mahalwari system were implemented. Thus, statement 4 is incorrect.

question_hi: रैयतवाड़ी बंदोबस्त के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?1. इसे थॉमस मुनरो द्वारा विकसित किया गया था।2. बंदोबस्त जमींदारों के साथ नहीं, बल्कि सीधे किसानों के साथ किया गया था।3. इसे टीपू के कब्जे वाले क्षेत्रों में छोटे पैमाने पर परीक्षण किया गया था।4. सफल होने पर, इसे गंगा के मैदानों में लागू किया गया था।सही संयोजन का चयन करें: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: What was the main motive of British colonial rule in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Social development of India
Industrialisation of India
Welfare of Indian farmers
Economic exploitation of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Economic exploitation of India

Explanation:
The main motive of British colonial rule in India was economic exploitation. The British extracted raw materials from India and sold finished goods in Indian markets, destroying local industries. Through land revenue systems and heavy taxation, they impoverished farmers. India was turned into a market for British goods and a source of cheap raw materials. Social development, industrialisation, or welfare of farmers were never the real objectives.

question: Pondicherry was captured by the Dutch in 1693 but was returned to the French company by the Treaty of Ryswick in _______. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1741
1704
1699
1696
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1699

Explanation:
Pondicherry was captured by the Dutch in 1693, which was a major blow to the French East India Company. However, under the Treaty of Ryswick signed in 1697, the Dutch returned Pondicherry to the French company. This treaty was concluded to end the Nine Years' War (1688–1697), which involved several European powers including France and England. According to the Treaty of Ryswick, most territories conquered during the war were restored to their original owners. Thus, Pondicherry was handed back to the French in 1699. The French East India Company later made Pondicherry its main center in India.

☛ Which treaty ended the Nine Years' War? → Treaty of Ryswick

question: This revolutionary freedom fighter co-founded the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in 1928. Along with B K Dutt, he threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929. He was tried and executed at the age of 23, along with revolutionaries Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru. The freedom fighter is: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Ramprasad Bismil
Bhagat Singh
Uddham Singh
Chandrasekhar Azad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bhagat Singh

Explanation:
Bhagat Singh, along with Sukhdev and Rajguru, was one of the most influential revolutionaries in the Indian independence movement. In 1928, he co-founded the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly to draw the government's attention. He was arrested and tried along with Sukhdev and Rajguru in the Lahore Conspiracy Case. All three were sentenced to death and executed on March 23, 1931, when Bhagat Singh was only 23 years old. Ramprasad Bismil was a leader of the Kakori Conspiracy. Chandrasekhar Azad was a co-founder of HSRA but died in a shootout at Alfred Park in 1931. Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in 1940.

☛ Date of execution → 23 March 1931

question: During the colonial period in India, the Vernacular Press Act (1878) was introduced by _____. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

Lord Wellesley
Lord Lytton
Lord Ripon
solution:

Explanation:
The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was introduced by Lord Lytton, the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880. This act aimed to tighten control over Indian language newspapers, which the British believed were criticizing the colonial government. It empowered district magistrates to prohibit the publication of any vernacular newspaper without a trial, making it known as the 'Gagging Act'. Lord Lytton's tenure also saw the outbreak of the Second Anglo-Afghan War and the passage of the Royal Titles Act of 1876. The act was heavily criticized by Indian nationalists as an attack on freedom of the press and was later repealed by Lord Ripon in 1882.

उन्होंने अपने लोगों को मुंडाओं का स्वर्ण युग वापस लाने की सलाह दी।

Explanation:
बिरसा मुंडा का जन्म 15 नवंबर 1875 को झारखंड (तत्कालीन बंगाल प्रेसीडेंसी) के रांची जिले के उलिहातू गाँव में हुआ था। वे मुंडा जनजाति से थे और उन्होंने अंग्रेजों और मिशनरियों के खिलाफ विद्रोह का नेतृत्व किया। उन्होंने लोगों से यूरोपीय लोगों को नष्ट करने और मुंडाओं का स्वर्ण युग वापस लाने का आग्रह किया था। वे स्थानीय मिशनरी स्कूल में भी शामिल हुए थे। इसलिए, मध्य प्रदेश के जंगलों में जन्म का कथन गलत है।

question: Who among the following sent a telegram on 6 August 1857 stating, 'Our men are cowed by the numbers opposed to them and the endless fighting. Every village is held against us, the zamindars have risen to oppose us'? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Lieutenant Colonel William Lambton
Lord Cornwallis
Lieutenant Colonel Tytler
Robert Clive
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lieutenant Colonel Tytler

Explanation:
Lieutenant Colonel Tytler sent this telegram from Delhi on 6 August 1857 during the Revolt of 1857, highlighting the difficulties faced by the British forces. The message indicates that the British were facing opposition from every village and the zamindars. Tytler was a British army officer in Delhi at the time and sent this telegram to Viceroy Lord Canning. In the telegram, he stated that his men were intimidated by the large numbers of rebels and the continuous fighting. This event is important for understanding the situation of the British administration during the Revolt of 1857. Tytler's message reflects the widespread impact of the revolt.

question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने 6 अगस्त 1857 को एक टेलीग्राम भेजा था, जिसमें कहा गया था, 'हमारे आदमी उनके विरोध में आने वाली संख्याओं और अंतहीन लड़ाई से डर गए हैं। हर गांव हमारे खिलाफ है, जमींदार हमारा विरोध करने के लिए उठ खड़े हुए हैं'? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: In which of the following cities was the Paramhansa Mandali founded to work for the abolition of caste? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Kanpur
Surat
Patna
Bombay
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bombay

Explanation:
The Paramhansa Mandali was founded in 1849 in Bombay (now Mumbai). Its aim was the abolition of caste system and social reform. The founder was Dadoba Pandurang. The organization emphasized monotheism and equality of all humans. Members had to follow rules like feeding Brahmins and dining with untouchables. The Mandali worked secretly and promoted women's education and widow remarriage. It later merged with the Prarthana Samaj.

question: In the context of British plantations in India, what does the term ‘bigha’ refer to? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: A unit of measurement of land
A plant that replaced indigo in Britain
An agreement made with the ryots
A revenue estate which has one or more villages
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A unit of measurement of land

Explanation:
In the context of British plantations in India, the term 'bigha' refers to a traditional unit of land measurement that varied across different regions of India. It was used during the Mughal and British periods for measuring agricultural land and determining revenue. The size of a bigha ranged from approximately 0.33 to 1 acre depending on the region. During British rule, it was used to measure land area for plantations such as indigo, tea, and coffee. This term does not refer to a plant, an agreement, or a revenue estate; it is strictly a unit of land measurement.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is a bigha a unit of? → Land measurement
☛ During the British period, what was the bigha used for? → Measuring land for plantations
☛ How many acres is one bigha approximately equal to? → 0.33 to 1 acre
☛ From which period has the term been in use? → Mughal period
☛ Is bigha an agreement or estate? → No, it is a land measurement unit

question: Who among the following strongly criticised British education for being too Western and disconnected from Indian realities? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Charles Wood
Rabindranath Tagore
Raja Rammohan Roy
Macaulay
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rabindranath Tagore

Explanation:
Rabindranath Tagore strongly criticised the British education system for being purely Western in its approach and disconnected from Indian realities, culture, and traditions. He believed that such education alienated students from their own roots and suppressed creativity and critical thinking. Tagore established an alternative education system at Shantiniketan, which emphasized nature, art, and Indian values. According to him, the purpose of education was not merely to secure jobs but to achieve holistic development of individuals. He opposed the compulsory use of English and the rote-learning method. His critique highlighted the need for an education system that respects local culture and fosters independent thought.

☛ What did Tagore consider the purpose of education? → Holistic development of individuals

question: Who among the following passed an Act in 1898, making it an offence to provoke people against the British rulers? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Lord Curzon
Lord Northbrook
Lord Elgin
Lord Mayo
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Curzon

Explanation:
In 1898, the Viceroy of India Lord Curzon passed an Act that made it an offence to provoke people against the British rulers. This Act came as an amendment to the Indian Penal Code and Code of Criminal Procedure. Its main objective was to suppress anti-British activities and crush the nationalist movement. It is also known as the Sedition Act. Lord Curzon's tenure lasted from 1899 to 1905. During this time, he also carried out the controversial Partition of Bengal in 1905. This Act was used to suppress many nationalist leaders.

question_hi: वह एक उग्र राष्ट्रवादी थे जिनका मानना था कि भारत की स्वतंत्रता का एकमात्र तरीका जन विरोध, विशेष रूप से युवाओं द्वारा है। इस उद्देश्य के लिए, उन्होंने गणेश चतुर्थी और शिवाजी जयंती जैसे स्थानीय त्योहारों को बड़े पैमाने पर मनाना शुरू किया, युवाओं से इसमें शामिल होने का आग्रह किया। वे 'केसरी' के संपादक भी थे, जो एक मराठी अखबार था, जो ब्रिटिश शासन के सबसे मजबूत आलोचकों में से एक बन गया। प्रश्न में नेता हैं: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)

गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले
solution_hi:

Explanation:
बाल गंगाधर तिलक एक प्रमुख भारतीय राष्ट्रवादी नेता थे जिन्होंने स्वराज (स्व-शासन) की वकालत की। उन्होंने ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ जन आंदोलन के साधन के रूप में गणेश चतुर्थी और शिवाजी जयंती जैसे सार्वजनिक उत्सवों की शुरुआत की। वे मराठी समाचार पत्र केसरी के संपादक थे, जो ब्रिटिश नीतियों का कड़ा आलोचक था। तिलक को उनके कट्टरपंथी दृष्टिकोण के लिए 'भारतीय अशांति के जनक' के रूप में जाना जाता था। उनका प्रसिद्ध नारा 'स्वराज मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है' ने जनता को प्रेरित किया। इस प्रकार सही उत्तर बाल गंगाधर तिलक हैं।
